propositions.text: Applicants seek judicial review of RAD decision under section 72 of IRPA
Judicial review concerns RAD appeal decision affirming RPD finding Applicants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection

paragraphs.summary: Applicants seek judicial review of RAD decision affirming RPD finding they are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection, under IRPA section 72.

propositions.text: RPD and RAD concluded Principal Applicant's credibility was determinative for all Applicants
Principal Applicant's testimony changed during RPD hearing and evolved on appeal with new evidence and allegations
Principal Applicant's wife and two children rely on his narrative for refugee claims

paragraphs.summary: RPD and RAD found Principal Applicant's credibility determinative; his testimony changed during RPD hearing and evolved on appeal with new evidence; family relies on his narrative.

propositions.text: RAD's decision was reasonable
RAD appropriately made findings on Principal Applicant's credibility and considered new evidence per IRPA and case law
Application for judicial review will be dismissed

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD's decision reasonable, properly considered credibility and new evidence, and dismisses application.

propositions.text: Applicants are Indian Sikh family; Principal Applicant was a farmer owning dairy farm in Karnal
Principal Applicant fears persecution from Indian police acting for Ms. Davinder Kaur (Gogi)
Gogi is sister of Principal Applicant's childhood friend Jatinder Singh and connected to army and ruling party

paragraphs.summary: Applicants are Indian Sikh family; Principal Applicant fears persecution from police acting for Gogi, sister of his childhood friend and politically connected.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant's fear stems from four incidents over two decades: 2001, 2010, 2017, and post-arrival in Canada
First incident in 2001 involved angering Gogi over adoption plan
2010 incident involved death threat after interfering in family property division
2017 incident involved police torture and false criminal charges bribed by Gogi
Post-arrival incident involved police issuing 'wanted notice' served on friend in 2019
Applicants arrived in Canada June 25, 2017 and sought refugee protection December 28, 2017

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant alleges four incidents causing fear: 2001 angering Gogi, 2010 death threat, 2017 police torture, and 2019 wanted notice; arrived Canada June 2017, claimed refugee December 2017.

propositions.text: Significant time gaps between alleged incidents are important as events themselves
Principal Applicant testified about 'minor incidents' during gaps but did not document them in BOC or amendments
Principal Applicant could not answer basic questions about nature and content of incidents during gaps at RPD hearing

paragraphs.summary: Court notes significant time gaps between incidents; Principal Applicant testified about minor incidents but did not document them and could not answer questions at RPD hearing.

propositions.text: In 2001, Principal Applicant alleges upsetting Gogi by opposing adoption of Jatinder's son by Gogi
Gogi has held grudge against Principal Applicant since 2001 incident

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant alleges in 2001 he upset Gogi by opposing adoption, causing her to hold a grudge.

propositions.text: No information about events from 2001 to 2010
In 2010, Gogi sought to reverse adoption after family argument; Principal Applicant involved and received death threat
Principal Applicant began fearing for his life in 2010

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant provides no events 2001-2010; alleges 2010 death threat after family dispute and began fearing for life then.

propositions.text: RPD sought details about 2010-2017 period; Principal Applicant said only 'small incidents' occurred
Principal Applicant claimed being followed in 2010 and 2014 but gave no details
RPD questioned why these events were not mentioned in BOC or amendments
Principal Applicant said incidents were small and only big incident in 2017 was mentioned

paragraphs.summary: RPD questioned 2010-2017 events; Principal Applicant said only small incidents, not in BOC; only 2017 big incident mentioned.

propositions.text: RPD identified inconsistencies in residency and travel history
Principal Applicant's forms and testimony conflicted on Karnal residence dates
Principal Applicant explained contradictions by interpreter error and mother's advice to move to Karnal after incidents

paragraphs.summary: RPD found inconsistencies in residency dates; Principal Applicant explained by interpreter error and mother's advice after incidents.

propositions.text: Applicants traveled to France and Eastern Europe in 2016 for tourism
Principal Applicant said he did not seek asylum during trips as no physical attack yet and situation was deescalating

paragraphs.summary: Applicants traveled to Europe in 2016; Principal Applicant said no asylum sought as no attack and situation was improving.

propositions.text: Applicants applied for temporary resident visas to Canada on April 9, 2017

paragraphs.summary: Applicants applied for Canadian temporary resident visas on April 9, 2017.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant involved in Sikh temple construction in Manchuri near Karnal
RPD noted no links to Manchuri and questioned importance and role in construction
Principal Applicant said land belonged to Sikh person and he had supervisory role collecting money
Principal Applicant said he was raising voice for poor Sikh community without details

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant involved in Sikh temple construction; RPD questioned role; he said supervisory role and raising voice for Sikhs.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant alleged local MLA delayed temple construction causing confrontation on April 28, 2017
Principal Applicant amended BOC to say Gogi was present and invited MLA to obstruct site
RPD asked why Gogi's presence was omitted initially; Principal Applicant did not answer
Principal Applicant said Gogi was on sidelines, others in forefront

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant alleged MLA delayed temple construction; amended BOC to add Gogi's presence; RPD questioned omission; Applicant said Gogi was on sidelines.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant claimed police tortured him at station on April 28, 2017 under Gogi's orders
He said he was detained overnight, beaten, questioned about Sikh terrorists and told to stop interfering

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant claimed police torture on April 28, 2017, detained overnight, beaten, questioned, and warned to stop interference.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant tendered medical report showing leg fracture and rod displacement from torture
He said he only realized injury severity after arriving in Montreal
RPD noted he did not mention leg injury earlier when questioned about torture injuries

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant submitted medical report of leg injury from torture; said he realized severity after arriving Montreal; RPD noted earlier omission.

propositions.text: Applicants obtained temporary resident visas May 2, 2017, less than a week after April 27-28 events
Applicants arrived Canada June 25, 2017 and sought refugee protection December 28, 2017

paragraphs.summary: Applicants got visas May 2, 2017, arrived Canada June 25, 2017, and claimed refugee protection December 28, 2017.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant asserted police issued 'wanted notice' served on friend in September 2019
RPD found photograph on wanted notice identical to one taken in Montreal December 2017
Principal Applicant said he did not know where police got photo and must have worn same clothes in April 2017

paragraphs.summary: Principal Applicant claimed police issued wanted notice in 2019; RPD found photo identical to Montreal 2017 photo; Applicant said he did not know origin and wore same clothes.

propositions.text: RPD denied refugee claim due to Principal Applicant's credibility deficiencies

RPD summarized credibility issues: warrant notice contradicted by evidence, improper service, identical photos, omission of Gogi's presence, unsatisfactory injury explanation, travel undermining fear, and contradictory residence claims

paragraphs.summary: RPD denied claim due to credibility issues including contradictory warrant notice, photo, omissions, injury explanation, travel, and residence inconsistencies.

propositions.text: Applicants appealed RPD decision on grounds of unfair hearing and erroneous credibility assessment

paragraphs.summary: Applicants appealed RPD decision alleging unfair hearing and errors in credibility assessment.

propositions.text: The decision under review is that of the Refugee Appeal Division.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the decision under review is that of the Refugee Appeal Division.

propositions.text: Applicants attached eight additional exhibits to the Principal Applicant's affidavit as new evidence on appeal before the RAD.
Section 110(4) IRPA governs admissibility of new evidence on appeal before the RAD, allowing only evidence arising after claim rejection or not reasonably available before.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the Applicants attached eight new exhibits on appeal and summarizes section 110(4) IRPA on admissibility of new evidence before the RAD.

propositions.text: The new evidence included five undated affidavits by neighbours, a letter by Jatinder Singh's son, a medical certificate dated Feb 9, 2021, and an excerpt from the Indian Code of Criminal Procedure.
Exhibit A: affidavit and letter by Neelam Notna about torture and harassment by police and advising not to return to India.
Exhibit B: affidavit by Amandeep Singh alleging Gogi's connections to army and politics.
Exhibits C, D, E: affidavits warning Principal Applicant against returning due to police search.
Exhibit F: letter by Akashdeep Singh describing father's gunshot wound in 2017.
Exhibit G: medical certificate confirming gunshot wound sustained in 2017.
Exhibit H: excerpt from Indian Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes the eight exhibits: five affidavits by neighbours, a letter by son, a medical certificate, and an Indian legal excerpt.

propositions.text: Three affidavits (Exhibits C, D, E) are identical except for addresses, signatures, and names.
These affidavits warn against returning to India due to police search and allege illegal detention and torture linked to Gogi's political connections.
Example affidavit text from Savinder Kaur is provided, showing similar content and verification statement.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes three affidavits are identical except for minor details and warns against returning to India due to police search linked to Gogi.

propositions.text: The RAD considered whether to admit the eight exhibits as new evidence applying criteria from Federal Court of Appeal decisions Singh (2016) and Raza (2007).
The RAD admitted only the excerpt from the Indian Criminal Code (Exhibit H).
Since Exhibit H was not central to the decision, the RAD did not hold an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD admitted only Exhibit H applying FCA criteria and did not hold an oral hearing as it was not central.

propositions.text: The RAD did not admit Exhibits A to G because they lacked credibility, reliability, or were reasonably available before claim rejection under subsection 110(4) IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD rejected Exhibits A to G for lacking credibility, reliability, or being reasonably available before claim rejection.

propositions.text: The credibility of Exhibits A to E was undermined by grammatical and spelling errors in the notary's official wet seal.
None of these documents were dated, further undermining credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD found Exhibits A to E lacked credibility due to errors in the notary seal and absence of dates.

propositions.text: Even if dated and error-free, the new evidence did not meet subsection 110(4) IRPA criteria as interpreted under Singh/Raza framework.

Singh (FCA) held admissibility under section 110(4) requires compliance with explicit provision and five implied conditions from Raza: credibility, relevance, newness, materiality, express statutory conditions.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the RAD found the evidence failed the Singh/Raza criteria of credibility, relevance, newness, materiality, and statutory conditions.

propositions.text: RAD held Exhibit A did not meet any Singh/Raza criteria but gave no fuller explanation.
RAD did not admit Exhibits B to F because it was unclear if events occurred after claim rejection or why evidence was not presented earlier.
Evidence could reasonably have been expected before RPD, so did not meet s.110(4) requirements.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD rejected Exhibits A to F for failing criteria and reasonable availability before RPD rejection.

propositions.text: Exhibit G, a medical certificate dated Feb 9, 2021, was issued before RPD claim rejection and thus inadmissible under s.110(4) IRPA.
RAD held it could have reasonably been presented before RPD hearing on May 4, 2021.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD rejected Exhibit G as it was issued before claim rejection and could have been presented earlier.

propositions.text: RAD declined to consider four new allegations in Principal Applicant's affidavit as they arose before RPD hearing.
Allegations involved Gogi's family in army, Gogi's husband's dangerousness, 2014 bicycle incident, and police obtaining photo from social media.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD declined four new allegations as they arose before the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: After admitting only one exhibit, RAD considered merits of appeal.
RAD held Applicants had a fair hearing and RPD did not err in assessing Principal Applicant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD found the Applicants had a fair hearing and no error in credibility assessment after admitting one exhibit.

propositions.text: RAD found no error in procedural steps of RPD hearing: opportunity to present evidence, interpreter, counsel, submissions, and reasons given.
RPD hearing lasted over two hours; determinative issues were stated; Principal Applicant given chance to explain; counsel made submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The court quotes RAD finding no procedural error in RPD hearing, which was fair and thorough with counsel and interpreter.

propositions.text: RAD found no reasonable apprehension of bias under Committee for Justice and Liberty test.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD found no reasonable apprehension of bias in the proceedings.

propositions.text: RAD made adverse credibility findings due to inconsistencies between testimony and BOC or amendments.
Credibility undermined by delay in leaving India despite death threat and travel abroad for tourism.
Credibility issues with testimony about Sikh temple construction and omissions about torture incidents.
Principal Applicant initially said MLA prevented construction; later said Gogi was present and brought MLA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD found multiple credibility issues with the Principal Applicant's testimony and omissions.

propositions.text: RAD upheld RPD's finding to give no weight to wanted notice with Principal Applicant's photo taken in Montreal.
Lack of explanation for how police obtained photo undermined document reliability and overall credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD rejected the wanted notice as unreliable and it undermined the Principal Applicant's credibility.

propositions.text: Applicants ask for judicial review and remittal to another decision maker.
Applicants argue RAD's refusal to admit new evidence was unreasonable.
Applicants argue admitted evidence would establish ongoing threat from Gogi and Indian state.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants seek judicial review, arguing the RAD unreasonably refused new evidence that would show ongoing threats.

propositions.text: Applicants rely on cases that minor typographical errors should not discredit legitimate documents.
Applicants cite Ali, Ayeni, and Enamejewa cases to argue spelling and grammatical errors in seal were minor.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants argue minor typographical errors should not discredit documents, citing relevant case law.

propositions.text: Applicants' counsel clarified that even if RAD's refusal to admit evidence was reasonable, the overall credibility assessment was unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants argue the RAD's overall credibility assessment was unreasonable even if refusal to admit evidence was reasonable.

propositions.text: Respondent seeks dismissal of judicial review application, asserting RAD decision was reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent seeks dismissal, arguing the RAD decision was reasonable.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably rejected affidavits and letters (Exhibits A to E) because they were undated and had significant errors on an official notary seal
Refers to Mohamed v Canada where RAD reasonably drew adverse inferences from errors in government documents
Mohamed v Canada found RAD reasonably considered inconsistencies and spelling mistakes on official documents to dismiss judicial review
Distinguishes Oranye case as it involved personal affidavits, not government stamps with spelling mistakes
Azenabor case found RAD's concerns about different fonts and typographical errors on official documents reasonable

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues RAD reasonably rejected undated affidavits with errors, citing Mohamed, Oranye, and Azenabor cases supporting RAD's findings on document credibility.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably refused to admit new evidence about gunshot wound to Jatinder Singh as it was available before RPD hearing

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues RAD reasonably refused new evidence on gunshot wound since it was available before RPD hearing.

propositions.text: Substance of evidence has little probative value; RAD's concerns about Applicants' lack of credibility are main hurdle

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues evidence has little probative value and RAD's credibility concerns are main obstacle to claim.

propositions.text: Standard of review is reasonableness as established in Vavilov, requiring justification, transparency, and intelligibility

paragraphs.summary: Court states standard of review is reasonableness per Vavilov requiring justification, transparency, and intelligibility.

propositions.text: Issues are whether RAD reasonably refused Applicants' evidence and whether RAD's decision was reasonable even if evidence inadmissible

paragraphs.summary: Court frames issues as whether RAD reasonably refused evidence and whether its decision was reasonable regardless.

propositions.text: Reasons must justify and explain outcomes to ensure transparency and intelligibility per Vavilov
Defective justifications fail transparency standard; reasons required for key elements especially with significant personal impact

paragraphs.summary: Court explains reasons must justify outcomes and be transparent, especially for key elements with personal impact per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reviewing courts must understand decision maker's reasoning but not substitute their own; must respect tribunal's delegated authority
Review for reasonableness is robust, not rubber stamping, despite principle of restraint

paragraphs.summary: Court states reviewing courts respect tribunal's reasoning and conduct robust reasonableness review without substituting views.

propositions.text: Federal Court of Appeal in Singh confirmed reasonableness standard applies to admissibility of new evidence
Subsection 110(4) conditions are essential before considering probative value or credibility

paragraphs.summary: Court notes FCA in Singh confirmed reasonableness standard and importance of subsection 110(4) conditions for new evidence admissibility.

propositions.text: Section 110(4) IRPA requires new evidence to emerge after RPD decision, be unavailable before, or not reasonably presented before
RAD must consider credibility, relevance, newness, and materiality when admitting new evidence

paragraphs.summary: Court states section 110(4) IRPA conditions and RAD's considerations for admitting new evidence.

propositions.text: RAD appeal is not opportunity to submit additional evidence to address RPD vulnerabilities
Applicants submitted new evidence to bolster credible threat argument in this case

paragraphs.summary: Court states RAD appeal not for new evidence to fix RPD issues; Applicants submitted new evidence to bolster claim.

propositions.text: RAD analyzed each new evidence piece and admitted only Indian Criminal Code passage (Exhibit H)
Remaining evidence could have been presented to RPD or was not credible or relevant
No reviewable errors found in RAD's rejection of affidavits, letter, and medical certificate

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably admitted only Exhibit H and properly rejected other evidence without error.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably found undated affidavits with grammatical and spelling errors lacked credibility
Official notary seal errors are serious, akin to misspelled government stamps as in Mohamed case
Affidavits could have been presented to RPD as they concern pre-hearing events, failing s.110(4) criteria

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably rejected undated affidavits with serious errors and that they could have been presented earlier.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably concluded letter and medical certificate failed s.110(4) criteria and lacked credibility and relevance
Evidence related to pre-hearing events and no adequate explanation for failure to present earlier

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably rejected letter and medical certificate as inadmissible and lacking credibility.

propositions.text: Not convinced RAD was unreasonable in finding new evidence inadmissible except Indian Criminal Code reference

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes RAD was reasonable in excluding new evidence except Indian Criminal Code passage.

propositions.text: Applicants did not raise procedural fairness concerns on judicial review though RAD addressed them on appeal
Procedural fairness issue not before the Court

paragraphs.summary: Court notes Applicants did not raise procedural fairness on review; issue not before Court.

propositions.text: Issue is whether RAD was reasonable in concluding Principal Applicant lacked credibility
RAD reasonably considered inconsistencies and contradictions in record to find Principal Applicant lacked credibility
Applicants failed to show RAD's credibility decision was unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably concluded Principal Applicant lacked credibility; Applicants failed to show unreasonableness.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably made adverse credibility finding due to unexplained identical photograph and late mention of Gogi

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably doubted credibility due to unexplained photograph and late mention of Gogi.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably found credibility undermined by omission of leg fracture and rod injury contradicting earlier testimony
Leg injury occurred weeks before departure to Canada and could not have been forgotten

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably doubted credibility due to omitted leg injury shortly before departure.

propositions.text: Applicant must show serious shortcomings in decision lacking justification, intelligibility, and transparency per Vavilov
Identified flaw must not be peripheral or superficial

paragraphs.summary: Court states applicant must show serious, non-peripheral flaws in decision lacking justification per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Lawani summarizes that credibility findings are entitled to deference and supported by contradictions if not peripheral
Microscopic or peripheral issues in testimony may constitute reviewable errors

paragraphs.summary: Court cites Lawani that credibility findings deserve deference unless based on peripheral issues, which may be reviewable errors.

propositions.text: Credibility findings on critical claim elements can extend to all evidence, using common sense and rationality.
Conclusions on witness credibility may be based on implausibilities, common sense, and human experience.
Findings must be sensitive to cultural differences.

paragraphs.summary: The court states credibility findings can extend to all evidence using common sense, implausibilities, and must be culturally sensitive.

propositions.text: Contradictions, omissions, and implausibilities in this case were significant.
Applicants argued there were shortcomings in the RAD decision making it unreasonable.
Applicants could not prove shortcomings in the RAD decision that would make it unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds significant contradictions and that applicants failed to prove RAD decision shortcomings making it unreasonable.

propositions.text: Judicial review application is dismissed.
No serious question of general importance was submitted by the parties.
No question is certified by the Court under s 74 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review application, finds no serious question of general importance, and certifies no question under s 74 IRPA.
